Healthy.description: The potato plant is healthy with no visible disease symptoms.

Early Blight.description: A fungal disease causing dark brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves.

cultural_practices: Rotate with non-host crops such as corn, soybean, and small grains for 2-3 seasons.
Remove weed hosts such as nightshade and horsenettle.
Practice fall tillage to bury infected crop residue.
Time irrigation to minimize leaf wetness duration.
Reduce plant stress through proper disease and nutrient management.
Store harvested tubers under conditions that promote rapid suberization.
monitoring: Begin field scouting once plants reach 12 inches in height.
Disease risk increases after 300 physiological days (P-Days) following crop emergence.
recommendations: Rotate fungicides with different FRAC groups to prevent resistance.
Ensure complete canopy coverage during spraying.

Late Blight.description: A highly destructive disease that rapidly spreads under cool and humid conditions.

sanitation: Destroy infected tubers and cull piles.
Bury infected material deep in soil.
Reduce inoculum sources around storage facilities.
healthy_seed: Sort and destroy infected tubers before storage.
Inspect seed tubers during harvesting and grading.
Keep harvested tubers in the field for 7-15 days before storage.
cultural_practices: Practice proper hilling and earthing up.
Destroy infected foliage 2-3 weeks before harvest.
Use wider row spacing to reduce humidity.
Orient rows toward sunlight when possible.

low_to_moderate_risk: Start spraying in the first week of November before disease appearance.
Apply Mancozeb, Kavach, Antracol or Blitox-50.
Up to 5 additional sprays may be required.
high_risk: Use Ridomil Gold, Curzate M-8, Sectin, Revus or Equation Pro as the 3rd and 4th sprays.
Maintain 10-day intervals between systemic fungicide sprays.
Follow with a protectant fungicide spray.
successive_or_spring_crop: Use Ridomil Gold as the first spray.

caution: Do not use reduced doses of Ridomil Gold.
Do not prepare self-made mixtures of Metalaxyl and Mancozeb.
Improper usage can lead to fungicide-resistant pathogen strains.
